key_insight: Neural transfer unification (NTU) lets a foundation decoder reuse knowledge across code distances, reducing the training bottleneck for large fault-tolerant quantum codes.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical path to scalable, amortized decoder training for quantum processors that need accurate decoding at larger code distances.
method: Align decoding tasks across distances using shared algebraic structure in scalable code families.
Train on smaller codes first, then transfer learned parameters to larger codes for faster adaptation.
Instantiate the framework as NTU-Transformer for planar surface codes and bivariate bicycle codes.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, NTU-Transformer is reported to beat correlation-aware matching on the [ [361,1,19] ] planar surface code, scale to [ [625,1,25] ] with transfer adaptation, and outperform Relay-BP on the [ [72,12,6] ] bivariate bicycle code in the low-physical-error regime.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on suitable algebraic alignment and transferability across code families, so results may not generalize without careful code-structure matching and tuning.
paper_title: Efficient foundation decoders for fault-tolerant quantum computing
